issue.title: RandomForest errors out with infinite values for predictions

llm_context.input_title: RandomForest errors out with infinite values for predictions
llm_context.input_body: No body provided in issue description.

generated_output.summary: RandomForest and other tree-based estimators in scikit-learn reject input data containing infinite values (`np.inf`), raising a ValueError. However, decision trees use simple inequality checks (`x <= value`) which are mathematically well-defined for infinite values, making this restriction unnecessary.
generated_output.root_cause_analysis: Input validation routines in scikit-learn enforce finiteness checks by default (via parameters like `ensure_all_finite=True`), rejecting infinite floating-point values before they can be evaluated by tree traversal rules.

step_by_step_plan.title: Inspect input validation functions for finiteness checks
step_by_step_plan.description: Examine check_array and related input validation helpers in sklearn/utils/validation.py to locate where ensure_all_finite evaluates infinite values for tree estimators.

step_by_step_plan.title: Review tree-based estimator prediction and fit methods
step_by_step_plan.description: Inspect BaseDecisionTree and related tree estimators in sklearn/tree/_classes.py to verify how input validation calls enforce finiteness during fit and predict.

step_by_step_plan.title: Adjust validation parameters for tree estimators
step_by_step_plan.description: Modify the input validation parameters or logic for tree-based models to permit infinite values (allow_inf=True or ensure_all_finite='allow-nan' equivalent or specific flag handling) so that infinite values pass validation.

step_by_step_plan.title: Add regression test for infinite values in tree predictions
step_by_step_plan.description: Add a new test case in sklearn/tree/tests/test_tree.py that fits a DecisionTreeClassifier/Regressor and a RandomForestClassifier/Regressor on data containing np.inf and asserts predictions are computed correctly without raising ValueError.

step_by_step_plan.title: Run test suite verification
step_by_step_plan.description: Run pytest on the tree test module using the suggested test command to verify that all existing tests pass and the new regression test succeeds.

structured_concepts.concept_name: Input Data Validation and Finiteness Checks
structured_concepts.short_explanation: Scikit-learn utility functions check user-supplied arrays for NaN and infinite values to prevent downstream numerical instability.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Ensures models do not encounter unexpected undefined mathematical operations during training or prediction.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Tree-based estimators invoke validation checks that reject infinite values even though tree decision rules (`x <= threshold`) can handle them.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: Decision trees make predictions by comparing feature values against fixed numerical split thresholds.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Comparisons like `infinity <= threshold` or `infinity > threshold` are well-defined in IEEE 754 floating-point arithmetic.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Because decision tree splits work naturally with infinite values, input validation should permit infinities for tree models where appropriate.

common_pitfalls: Globally disabling finiteness checks across all estimators, which would break linear models and distance-based algorithms where infinity causes NaNs or overflow.
Forgetting to update tags or input validation parameters specific to tree-based estimators.
